result.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
result.summary: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging.

AI.brief_summary: G0.7 是面向机器人控制的世界动作模型，基于 Fast-WAM 把观测上下文扩展到五分钟并大规模预训练于遥操作与人类自我中心视频，使推理时跳过未来帧生成、直接解码动作，从而支持实时闭环控制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「训练期用未来帧预测塑形策略表示、推理期省略生成」的设置，可能为 LVR 中轨迹监督如何影响 latent 状态的实际使用、以及省略显式生成后的收益与代价提供核查线索；但任务是动作控制而非视觉推理，需确认其是否有表示层面的分析。
